content.text:
I built the Markdown wiki described in SPEC.md, and `node --test` passes: 3 of 3, which is the public smoke test plus two test files of my own. I also checked the renderer against the official CommonMark 0.31.2 examples. Every example I compared matched after the whitespace and `
`/`` normalisation the spec allows. I skipped the raw-HTML examples, because the spec deliberately changes that behaviour. **What I reused and what I wrote** - **Reused:** the Markdown parser. Writing a CommonMark-compliant parser from scratch is large and easy to get wrong. markdown-it 14.1.0 (MIT) ships a single file containing all its dependencies, and it already supports pipe tables and `~~strikethrough~~`. I copied that file unchanged to `src/vendor/markdown-it.cjs` and load it with Node's standard library, so there are no npm dependencies. It's recorded in `PROVENANCE.json`, and all the license notices are in `src/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. - **Wrote myself:** everything specific to this spec. It was quicker to write than to find and adapt. **What's in `src/`** - **`markdown.js`** provides `render`, `toc` and `slugify`, plus a helper that lists a page's wiki-link targets. - Raw HTML comes out as escaped text. - Links using `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `file:` or `data:` become `#`, except `data:` images in png, gif, jpeg or webp. - Strikethrough renders as ``. - Headings get GitHub-style ids, with `-1`, `-2` added to duplicates. - `[[Page]]` and `[[target|label]]` become links, marked `missing` when the page doesn't exist. They aren't converted inside code. - **`server.js`** has every route in the spec, with the specified error format and status codes (400, 404, 409). - Each page and its full history is saved as one JSON file under `dataDir/pages/`, so data survives a restart. - Saves are versioned, and saving unchanged content doesn't create a new version. - Also covered: conflict checks with `baseVersion`, history, revert, backlinks and links, tags, export/import, and the standalone `/wiki/:slug` pages. - Update times always increase, even for saves in the same millisecond, so "newest first" sorting is reliable. - **`diff.js`** does the line-by-line diff, with removed lines listed before added ones in each changed block. - **`public/`** is the browser app: - page list with tag filter and sort - search with highlighted snippets - editor with a live preview and table of contents - saving that warns on conflicts and lets you reload or overwrite - history with revert and diff - backlinks panel - **`main.js`** starts the server using `PORT` (default 3000) and `DATA_DIR` (default `./data`). I started it once and confirmed it serves the app. **Where the spec was ambiguous, I chose:** - An empty page body counts as zero lines in a diff. - A diff with no `from`/`to` compares the previous version with the current one. - `baseVersion` is ignored when a page is first created. - Revert always creates a new version, even if the content is unchanged. - When a search matches only the title, the snippet is the first 80 characters of the body. - A search result's `score` is the number of matches in the title and body combined.
